140-program-description: Principles of ecological agriculture, for those who want to farm, work in extension or government, or study further. It may take more than 90 credits with your major.
In U1, talk to your major's adviser and the Minor's. Declare when registering for U2, and the Minor's adviser certifies which courses count.
140-general-regulations: C or better; at least 24 credits, at most 6 shared with your major (electives excluded).
140-program-description-2: Close to the Minor, for agrologists wanting further training and formal recognition. Needs a B.Sc. in agriculture or a related area, and you can't take it after the Minor or specialization.
140-general-regulations-2: At least 30 credits. Most 300+ courses have prerequisites. AGRI 310 used here must be on an organic, biodynamic or permaculture enterprise, with the adviser's approval.
142-about-the-institute-of-parasitology: One of Canada's oldest interdisciplinary research centres, on parasites, their hosts and limiting parasitic disease. No undergraduate degree now; graduate programs and certificates are on its site.
143-about-the-department-of-plant-scienc: Plant scientists tackle feeding a growing population, climate change, scarce water and lost biodiversity. The Department helps train agrologists, ecologists, botanists and biotechnologists (see p. 91).
143-program-description: Lets students in other majors earn credit in agricultural production. It may take more than 90 credits with your major.
See both advisers in first year, declare when registering for your second-last year, and the Minor's adviser certifies your courses. Most 300+ courses have prerequisites, and not all run yearly.
144-program-description: Not currently offered. A 12-month diploma on ethical, medical and legal issues, medicinal chemistry, contaminants and products, production, breeding and disease, with an industry internship.
144-program-description-2: Biology, breeding, propagation and management of crops and vegetables, under the Sustainable Agricultural Systems Major. Adding Professional Agrology meets OAQ eligibility.
144-program-description-3: Agriculture as a tool for rural development, reducing poverty and food security worldwide. Taken with the Sustainable Agricultural Systems Major; adding Professional Agrology meets OAQ eligibility.
145-program-description: Not currently offered. How soils and water interact in urban and farm landscapes: conservation, watershed decisions and remediation. With Professional Agrology, it would meet OAQ requirements.
145-complementary-courses-9-credits: BREE 529 or ENVB 529 counts, but not both.
145-program-description-2: Knowledge and hands-on experience to improve agriculture: ecological stewardship, innovative farming and food security, with field work. With the Professional Agrology Specialization, you can join the OAQ.
145-complementary-courses-21-credits: 6–12 credits (3–6 from two of three groups), not counted toward your specialization too.
146-livestock: 0–15 credits from a further list, and 0–9 credits for those applying to the OAQ.
147-minor-programs: Offered by the Dean's Office or with partners.
147-minor-in-environmental-engineering: 21 credits of environment courses, reachable with as few as 12 extra credits for Bioresource Engineering students. Run by Civil Engineering (p. 812).
147-minor-in-field-studies-barbados-inte: With the University of the West Indies each summer at the Bellairs Research Institute: three 3-credit courses and a 6-credit project on sustainable food, energy and nutrition, with projects of national importance. See p. 1194.
147-minor-in-management-for-non-manageme: Offered by Desautels to add managerial skills.
147-program-description: A practical global view of agriculture for rural development, poverty and food security, combining McGill courses with field experience in a developing country. Costs vary.
149-africa-field-study-semester: East Africa each January, natural and social sciences, from desert to rainforest and villages to cities.
149-barbados-field-study-semester: 15 credits each Fall at Bellairs Research Institute (p. 1286).
149-barbados-interdisciplinary-tropical-: 15 credits each summer, living at Bellairs and studying there and at UWI (p. 1286).
149-panama-field-study-semester: 15 credits, January to April, with the Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute: an internship or research project on practical environmental problems in Panama.
150-about-the-faculty-of-arts: Founded in 1843 and McGill's largest faculty: 15 departments, 4 schools, 4 institutes and 12 research centres, with over 350 full-time academics, about 8,000 undergraduates and over 1,100 graduate students.
Centred on the McCall MacBain Arts Building, McGill's oldest, plus Leacock, Ferrier, Peterson, Morrice, Wilson, Birks and 680 Sherbrooke West. The Dean's Office is in Dawson Hall.
Exchanges worldwide, and the Internship Office helps over 200 students a year work with organizations around the globe.
150-administrative-officers: Lisa Shapiro, Dean. Associate Deans: Michael Fronda (Budget and Administration), Cecily Hilsdale (Graduate), Sonia Laszlo (Research and EDI), Heidi Wendt (Student Affairs), Manuel Balán (Curriculum and Faculty Affairs, from January 2026). Richard Courtois, Director of Administration.
A B.A. requires completing at least one Arts program.
151-faculty-admission-requirements: For the B.A., B.A. & Sc., B.S.W. and B.Th., see the Undergraduate Admissions Guide. Transfers: p. 39 and Arts OASIS.
151-advising: Know the rules. Advisers help, but correctness of your choices is your responsibility, and misunderstanding earns no exemption.
96 or fewer credits to go: get course approval from an adviser in your department. 97–120: you're normally in a Foundation Program for the first year, and see Arts OASIS.
151-faculty-of-arts-office-of-advising-a: Arts OASIS, ground floor of Dawson Hall, advises on programs, requirements, standing, transfers, Study Away and graduation, and supports you through personal, financial or medical trouble. Book online.
151-degree-requirements-for-the-faculty-: Your responsibility, as above. For a B.A., finish at least one Arts program within your Multi-Track, Honours or Joint Honours requirement, plus all Faculty and program requirements.
152-definitions: Units: departments or equivalents. Programs: lists of required and complementary courses. Major Concentration: typically 36 credits. Minor Concentration: typically 18.
152-foundation-program-overview: With 0–23 credits of Advanced Standing (97+ to go), you start in the Foundation Year before choosing a program, selecting an option in Minerva.
152-regulations: Core courses need C or better, and U0 can't use S/U. Advanced Standing may count. With 96 or fewer credits to go, choose your programs when you register.
152-multi-track-requirement: Usually two components in different subjects: Major + Minor, Major + Major, Honours + Minor, or Joint Honours + Joint Honours. A Faculty Program is exempt.
152-regulations-2: At least one component must come from an Arts unit. A Major or Honours from outside Arts must pair with an Arts Major or Minor. A Joint Honours component from outside pairs with an Arts one, or with another outside one plus an Arts Minor.
152-honours-program-requirements: More focused than a Major, typically 48–60 credits with special courses, preparing you for graduate study.
152-regulations-3: Needs GPA and CGPA of 3.00 in the previous year to stay in, unless the department and Associate Dean allow otherwise. Finish with CGPA 3.00 and program GPA 3.00, or higher if the unit says.
You also need a Minor in another subject, except in Honours Faculty Programs and the Spécialisation enrichie Langue et littérature françaises.
153-joint-honours-program-requirements: Two subjects at a high level, each usually 36 credits (30–48), with high marks in program and elective courses.
153-regulations: Same 3.00 rules for staying in and finishing, with the program GPA met in both components. It satisfies Multi-Track if one is from Arts, with no Minor needed.
153-faculty-program-requirements: Interdisciplinary concentrations of usually 54+ credits, exempt from Multi-Track: Environment, and Population and Global Health (from 2026–2027).
153-other-options-science-minor-programs: You can add an approved Science Minor with its prerequisites. For programs in other faculties, see OASIS and p. 155.
153-program-requirements: A broad base for the three-year degree, 24–30 credits. In the French option, up to 18 credits are in French, in language courses, content courses or both.
153-degree-requirements-b-a-students: Faculty and program requirements on p. 151; see an OASIS adviser for planning.
153-core-requirement-18-credits: 18 credits in French Language and Literature and French as a Second Language, by proficiency.
153-french-as-a-second-language-frsl: Up to 12 credits of intensive courses (6 credits a term each). Introductory students take at least 6 credits in Foundation and may finish in U1.
154-substantive-content-courses-taught-i: Subject courses taught in French count when they are; POLI 226 alternates between languages.
154-remaining-credits-12-credits: Normally 12, from the approved Foundation list on Arts OASIS.
154-program-requirements: Build your own program of 24–30 credits. The core is 6 credits in each of three of four categories (social sciences, humanities, languages, math and science), plus 12 approved credits. At most 18 in one area and 12 from one department.
154-core-requirement-18-credits: 6 credits in each of three of the four categories, from lists of courses approved for U0.
154-approved-courses-social-sciences: See OASIS. Some, like CANS 200 and ISLA 210, also count as humanities.
154-approved-courses-humanities: See OASIS. Some need university prerequisites and don't suit a first term, and some count in other categories.
154-approved-courses-languages: See OASIS. D1 needs its D2 too. Take at most one language at introductory level; with prior knowledge, take higher levels with permission.
155-approved-courses-mathematics-and-sci: See OASIS. Check prerequisites. GEOG 205 is also a social science.
155-course-requirements: C or better in program courses. If you fall short in a required course, pass the supplemental or repeat it, normally once. See OASIS before a third attempt.
A failed complementary can be replaced. A D then still counts as an elective. Repeating a required D course gives credit only once.
155-course-prerequisites: Arts won't block you, but ask the instructor if you lack one. Other faculties may block you.
155-course-overlap: No extra credit for courses overlapping earlier credit from McGill, CEGEP, another university, AP, A-Levels, IB or French Baccalaureate. Check with OASIS, SOUSA or the department.
Double-prefix courses: take your own department's version if offered together, otherwise whichever fits. Computer course credit follows each course's own rules.

Science and B.A. & Sc. students need the Associate Dean's permission for statistics from other faculties (except B.Sc. Environment's required ones), and for outside computer courses, only exceptionally.

Only one introductory statistics course counts, and only one intermediate. Credit for PSYC 204, MATH 324 or MATH 357 rules out the lower ones listed. PSYC 305 can go with ECON 227 or 257. For other 500-level statistics, check with an adviser.
156-credit-limit-for-courses-outside-the: Maximum 12 credits outside Arts and Science over your degree, or 30 in designated programs, 39 if you combine them.

Designated: minors in Education for Arts Students, Educational Psychology, Entrepreneurship and Management for Non-Management Students, Field Studies, Geography Urban Studies, and music subjects; Geography Urban Studies major and honours; Environment honours and Faculty Program; Population and Global Health; Joint Honours in Economics with Accounting or Finance, who can't take Desautels minors.

Continuing Studies courses starting with C don't count. Courses listed in Arts or Science sections, and approved Field Study courses, count as Arts or Science. Limits are strictly enforced, with excess courses flagged as no credit after add/drop.
A minor from another faculty that isn't on the approved list needs Faculty permission, which isn't guaranteed.
157-inter-university-transfer-credit-pol: From a faculty outside Arts and Science elsewhere: up to 30 credits, C or better only (no C-, P or S). The original faculty decides how it's classed. Continuing Education courses count only if they led to a degree.
At McGill you can take more outside courses only if you transferred under 12 credits, up to 12. Programs requiring more are capped at 39 in all.
157-interfaculty-transfer-credit-policy-: Moving to the B.A.: all Arts and Science credit, plus up to 30 outside credits with D or better, with grades remaining in GPA. Same 12 and 39 limits.
157-definition-of-online-courses-for-tra: A course is online if more than 20% is delivered online.
157-credit-limit-for-online-courses: At most 6 credits through Independent Study Away, as electives, from an accredited degree-granting institution, counting toward its degrees, with Arts OASIS's prior approval. They count toward your term maximum.
158-exceptions: Exchange and IUT aren't limited, and courses transfer the same way whether online or not, though in-person is advised abroad.
Science decides for CHEM, COMP, ENVR, GEOG, MATH, PHYS and PSYC; Desautels for BUSA, INSY, FINE, MGCR, MGPO, MGSC, MRKT and ORGB.
158-internship-courses: Offered for credit; see the Arts Internship Program.
158-courses-in-academic-english-for-engl: If English isn't your primary language and you've had under five years in English secondary school, up to 12 credits of WCOM. Most need a placement test, and the Writing Centre then gives a permit.
158-first-year-seminar-courses: For first-year U0 or U1 students, first-come, first-served, 25 at most. Take one only. Lists on p. 167 (Arts) and p. 1107 (Science).
158-graduate-level-courses: B.A. students can ask for 600-level courses with CGPA 3.30, in U3 or higher, written approval from the professor and adviser, up to 6 credits, if there's room. Not 700 or 800, and not Visiting, Special or Exchange students.
Same standards as graduate students. The form is on OASIS.
158-minimum-credit-requirement: As in your admission letter. Transfers need 60 McGill credits. Readmitted students follow the current requirements; after five years away, possibly 60 new credits and a new GPA, or fewer if approved.
159-recognition-and-maxima-for-advanced-: Normally 120 credits, with up to 30 for DEC, IB, French Baccalaureate, A-Levels, AP or college courses taken with high school. Declare AP scores of 4 or 5 when first registering.
No credit for overlaps or for study abroad intermediaries. You may still do 120 McGill credits, with limits on repeating exempted courses.
159-residency-requirement: At least 60 credits at McGill, and two-thirds of each program. Departments may require more.
On approved exchange, up to half of a minor can be done elsewhere. Diploma in Environment: 30 credits.
159-time-and-credit-limit-for-completion: With 96 or fewer to go, finish within eight terms; Foundation students start the count after a year. B.A. requirements should fit within 120 credits.
Beyond that semester, you need Faculty permission, normally only for valid academic or immigration reasons, and only needed courses then count.
159-examinations: Tentative schedule about a month into term, final about two months. Don't book travel before the exam period ends.
